pages.x: In 1952 Fulgencio Batista seized power in Cuba in a coup. His Havana was a playground of casinos run by American gangsters, while many Cubans in the countryside lived in poverty, and American companies owned much of the island's sugar, mines and land.

On 26 July 1953 a young lawyer, Fidel Castro, led about 160 rebels in an attack on the Moncada army barracks in Santiago de Cuba. It failed, and most were killed or captured. At his trial Castro spoke for hours and ended with the words history will absolve me. He was let out in an amnesty two years later.

In December 1956 Castro sailed back from Mexico with 82 men crammed onto an old yacht, the Granma. Most were killed or captured soon after landing, but a handful escaped into the Sierra Maestra mountains, among them Castro's brother Raúl and an Argentine doctor, Che Guevara.

From the mountains the rebels won over the peasants and fought Batista's army, which lost heart. In December 1958 Che Guevara's column captured an armoured train at Santa Clara. On New Year's Eve Batista fled the country, and in January 1959 Castro's bearded rebels rode into Havana in triumph.

Castro took over American-owned land, sugar mills, banks and oil refineries, and had hundreds of Batista's men executed. When the United States cut off trade, he turned to the Soviet Union, which bought Cuba's sugar and sold it oil. In 1961 he declared that Cuba was socialist.

In April 1961 some 1,400 Cuban exiles, trained and armed by the American CIA, landed at the Bay of Pigs to overthrow Castro. The rising they hoped for never came, and within three days they were killed or captured. It was a humiliation for the new American president, John F. Kennedy.

Castro ruled Cuba for almost 50 years. His government gave Cubans free schools and health care and wiped out illiteracy, but jailed its critics and allowed no free elections, and over a million Cubans left, many for Florida. The American embargo still stands, and the Communist Party still rules.
pts: Batista fled on New Year's Day 1959
The Bay of Pigs invasion failed in 1961
